react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, Mummichog m/z-directed activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — converged on cholesterol homeostasis and primary bile acid biosynthesis as the dominant pathway disruption. Cholesterol (KEGG:C00187) was the most frequently recurring driver, appearing as the sole member hit in the RaMP Reactome 'Intestinal lipid absorption' (FDR=0.0027), as a 5-member overlap in Mummichog's 'Bile acid biosynthesis' (p=0.018, rank 1 of 15), and in MetaboAnalystR's KEGG hsa00100 Steroid biosynthesis (p=0.099, rank 1 of 5). The KEGG hsa00120 Primary bile acid biosynthesis pathway was also detected (MetaboAnalystR rank 2, p=0.111). Secondary convergence appeared around purine metabolism, where uric acid (C00366) contributed a rank-10 hit in Mummichog (p=0.048) and appeared in RaMP's 'Disorders of transmembrane transporters' (FDR=0.0017). Vitamin B6 metabolism showed up via 4-pyridoxic acid (C00847) in RaMP (FDR=0.0027) and MetaboAnalystR (rank 1, p=0.022). The Phase I xenobiotic biotransformation cluster (Cytochrome P450 substrates) was enriched in RaMP (R-HSA-211897, FDR=0.0017; R-HSA-211945, FDR=0.0027), driven by coumarin (C05851), N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319), and benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (C14853). The treatment group thus exhibits a coordinated perturbation spanning steroid-to-bile acid conversion, urate clearance, and oxidative xenobiotic metabolism, consistent with exposure to lipophilic environmental toxicants causing secondary disruption of lipid-soluble vitamin handling and nucleobase excretion.
